newsitem.title: USA: Possis says Q3 Angiojet sales $1.05 mln.
newsitem.headline: Possis says Q3 Angiojet sales $1.05 mln.

text.p: Possis Medical Inc said Tuesday that worldwide AngioJet System sales for the fiscal third quarter ended April 30 were about $1.05 million, compared with $166,000 in the fiscal second quarter.
U.S. AngioJet sales were about $651,000 in the third quarter, Possis said.

The AngioJet is a medical device that washes away blood clots inside arteries, bypass grafts and veins. The device was cleared for marketing by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in December 1996 with labeling claims for removal of blood clots from grafts used in kidney dialysis.
Possis said it has increased its AngioJet sales staff to 14 from six and two more clinical specialists are expected to be added this quarter.
Possis said it has 25 AngioJet drive-unit purchase proposals under hospital review.
"Although no drive unit proposals have cleared the review process, none have been rejected and several appear to be nearing approval," said chief executive Robert Dutcher.
"I'm hopeful drive unit sales will commence this quarter ... The AngioJet drive unit sales cycle appears to be longer than the three-six months we originally estimated," he said.

"Drive units are capital equipment and go through a more rigorous budgeting/purchasing process than disposable products. In addition, with our U.S. marketing clearance coming in December 1996, many 1997 capital budgets had already been established," Dutcher said.
Shares in the Minneapolis-based medical devices maker opened unchanged at 16-1/4.
